Evans, 12 


To build stronger communities 
by providing opportunities for everyone 
to lead fulfilling, active, healthy and engaged lives. 


MISSION 


This Community Report 
is not only about the YMCA. 


This Community Report 

is first and foremost about 
the difference YOU are 
making in people’s lives. 


Maybe it doesn't seem 
like much... And yet! 


For a child who is on 
his own after school, 


For a young person 
who is having serious 
problems at home, 


For a sedentary adult 
who can go a week 
without seeing anyone, 


For a family who can’t afford 
activities for their children, 


It means a lot. 


We couldn't 
change lives 
without you 


- OUR DONORS, VOLUNTEERS, 
EMPLOYEES AND PARTNERS - 


are giving children 
who are struggling a chance 
to succeed in school and in life. 


are getting kids off the street 
and allowing them to reach 
their full potential. 


are encouraging adults 
and families 

to stay active and connect 
with their community. 


are lending a hand 

to all these people when they 
need it most, and are helping 
them overcome life’s challenges. 


Stéphane Vaillancourt — President and CEO, The YMCAs of Québec 


Waguih Rabbat - Chair of the Board of Directors, The YMCAs of Québec 


Gregory Chrispin—President, YMCAs of Québec Foundation 


Québec’s youth are becoming 

less fit and more prone to illnesses 
like diabetes. This is a real public 
health issue. We must act now and 
encourage more young people to 
get moving in our programs. 


E xperts are sounding the alarm: 


“December 21, 2016—On this day, 

at the age of 21, | was diagnosed with 
Type 1 Diabetes. This meant a lifetime 
sentence of constantly monitoring 

my sugar intake and giving myself at least 
four injections of insulin a day. If | wasn’t 
careful, my future could include limb 
amputations, vision loss, and even death. 


| was encouraged to incorporate 

some physical activity into my schedule 
to keep my sugar levels in check. In doing 
so, | was able to not only improve my 
physical well-being, but also to alleviate 
the mental burden of being diagnosed 
with a chronic disease. 


Now, | realize that the YMCA was more 
than just a way for me to get into shape. 
It was a place that empowered me to 
take the disease into my own hands.” 


“The YMCA 
is where 


| 


Se 


| conquered 


my diabetes.” 


Karmin 


Thanks to your help, YMCA members 

are not only improving their physical skills, 
but also gaining the self-confidence, 
motivation, and knowledge they need to 
make physical activity part of their daily lives. 


uébec youth are facing 

several challenges: a high school 

dropout rate, sedentary behaviour, 
technology addiction, bullying, and 
marginalization. This is why it is so 
important to provide young people 
with a safe place where they can be 
active, learn and make connections. 


HELPING 
aaa 


With your support, the Y can give 

young people what they need 

to make positive choices and succeed. 
Interacting with caring adult role models 
and participating in rewarding activities 
creates a climate of trust and a sense of 
belonging that@ncourages youthitortalk 
about their problems, big and small. 


When people think of an at-risk youth, 
what often comes to mind is someone who 
is aggressive, gets kicked out of class, or is 
in trouble with the police. But an at-risk 
youth can also be quiet and withdrawn... 


Isolation, a lack of resources, problems at 
school... these are some of the risk factors 
that could have turned young Kared into 
one more statistic. 


But, after only six months in the YMCA 
Plusone Mentoring program, Kared is more 
self-confident and independent, and feels 
less isolated. All thanks to having his mentor 
Kilsaris by his side. 


“| feel more free 
because | wasn’t 
doing anything 


at home. | felt like 
| was In a cage.” 


Kared, 10 


he news reminds us every day that 

we live in a time when social cohesion 

is fragile. More than ever, we must 
work towards creating a climate of fairness, 
inclusion, empathy and respect. 


“Here, people feel 
like themselves.” 


Emanuel, Street Worker

“| arrived in Boston on a Friday. The Opera House 
was closed. | spent three days on the street. 

Without warm clothes or money. The YMCA took 

me in. Thanks to the YMCA, | survived my first winter.

Kent Nagano, Honorary Laureate, 2017 YMCA Peace Medals
